description:
FOUND AND MEASURED at fz-kdt.13.2, deliberately NOT changed there.

THE SEAM. A non-rebased conclusion of `AnalyzeActivation` keeps every `Activation`/`ActivationInputs`/`CallSiteSummary`/`CallSiteTargets` claim it could not re-derive (fz-kdt.63, absence is bottom) and REPLACES its read set with the one this run recorded. So a preserved claim keeps standing while the subscriptions that justified it are dropped. The ledger then answers 'can this fact still move?' from evidence that no longer covers it -- optimistic finality, and premature-settledness is the fatal failure class (fz-kdt.13's strategy).

This predates the answer split: at job granularity the same conclusion replaced the JOB's reads while preserving the job's claims. The split does not make it unsound, it makes it FINER: a callsite answer's replacement set is a short prefix, not the whole run's read vector, so the same drop is more likely to lose a live edge.

WHY IT IS PROBABLY BENIGN TODAY (the frontier argument, not a proof): a run that could not re-derive a claim either blocked -- and a satisfied WAIT dirties every answer the job holds, since a wait carries no derivation attribution -- or concluded with the callsite resolving to nothing, which depends on values that came from facts it DID read. Progress past that state needs the recorded frontier to move first.

THE FIX THAT WAS TRIED AND BACKED OUT. Union the answer's standing reads into its reported reads whenever it preserved a claim ('keeping a claim means keeping its subscriptions'). Sound -- strictly more subscriptions -- and cheap. Measured cost, release `fz2 interp`, settled-at-end off the public stream:

  fixture               kind              faithful -> with union
  fz_f98_range_map      Activation             37 ->  12
  fz_f98_range_map      CallSiteTargets        35 ->  11
  enum_take_drop_split  Activation            131 -> 107
  enum_take_drop_split  CallSiteTargets       264 -> 246
  enum_predicate_search Activation            133 -> 114
  AnalyzeActivation evaluations: 1058 -> 1065 (take_drop), 766 -> 769 (predicate), 306 -> 306 (range_map); `report.uncaused` stayed empty, so the extra work is caused.

Preservation is common (it is what fz-kdt.63 exists for), so the union makes a preserving answer accumulate its whole history of reads and collapses its finality back toward job granularity -- it trades optimistic finality for pessimistic finality and costs most of the precision the split buys. Neither end of that trade is TRUTHFUL, which is why it wants a real design rather than a switch.

WHAT A REAL FIX LOOKS LIKE: per-CLAIM provenance, so a preserved claim carries the reads that produced it and only those rejoin the answer's read set. That is the only formulation that is both sound and precise. Cost it against just retiring preservation (give the analysis a way to say 'this callsite is unresolved' as content rather than as silence), which would remove the seam entirely.
title: A preserved claim keeps its claim but loses its subscriptions
